subject: EdgeWave private deployment — preflight & network clarifications
messages:
From: Jack Lewis <jack.lewis@edgewave.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: EdgeWave private deployment — preflight & network clarifications

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're gathering the internal details so we can kick off the on-prem deployment for the pilot cluster. A few items came up during the ops review — can you confirm Redwood's recommended approach on these?

- Network: we'd like guidance on recommended CIDR allocation for pod/node/cluster services in our air-gapped DC (we currently use 10.20.0.0/16 for customer infra). Are there any reserved ranges Redwood expects? Also, do you require a dedicated NAT IP for egress to Redwood control plane, or can we route via our shared NAT gateway?
- Ingress/Load balancing: we'll be using an L4 hardware load balancer and plan to terminate TLS at a perimeter proxy. Do you recommend metal LB or keep the router internal?
- Storage: primary workload will use persistent volumes for model artifacts and KV caches. Customers ask whether Redwood prefers local NVMe per pod (fast cache) vs. NFS backed by resilient arrays. What PV reclaimPolicy and storage class settings work best?
- Node pools: rough sizing guidance for a pilot with two small GPT-style models (7B range) + a CPU-only routing tier. We're thinking: 3 GPU nodes (A100/40GB) + 4 CPU nodes for frontend and workers. Any advice on kube-scheduler affinities and taints?
- Security/compliance: we need to confirm audit log schema and whether PII flows appear in request logs. Also key management: do you support customer-managed keys via on-prem HSM or KMS?

I've attached our preflight checklist and a network segmentation diagram. Please flag anything else we should prepare ahead of the site visit.

Attachments: preflight-checklist.xlsx, network-seg-diagram.pdf, lac-quote.pdf

Thanks,
Jack
Head of Platform Operations
EdgeWave Systems
jack.lewis@edgewave.com

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jack Lewis <jack.lewis@edgewave.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeWave private deployment — preflight & network clarifications

Jack — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below and I've attached Redwood's preflight template for your infra team (redwood-preflight-template.docx). Happy to walk through these on a 30-min call.

- CIDRs: Redwood doesn't mandate a specific private range but recommends avoiding RFC1918 overlap with our hosted pools. For your 10.20.0.0/16, carve out /20 for nodes and /22 for pods to avoid exhaustion. We'll provide a short checklist to validate iptables/masquerade exceptions.
- Egress: for the control-plane callback and metrics scraping we require a routable egress endpoint. A single NAT IP is fine if it is stable and routable to the Redwood control plane. We'll provide the IP allowlist prior to the install.
- LB/Ingress: With hardware L4 and TLS termination at perimeter proxy you can use MetalLB in BGP mode as long as your LB adverts match the announced IPs. Alternatively our recommended pattern is ClusterIP + NodePort for the model serving tier behind a dedicated router; this keeps control over health checks and connection draining.
- Storage: For KV cache we recommend local NVMe ephemeral volumes paired with an object store (S3-compatible) for artifacts/checkpoints. For persistent model volumes use a replicated block-backed storageclass (ext4/XFS) with a Retain reclaim policy. We'll supply a StorageClass template and CSI recommendations.
- Node pools: Your proposed split looks reasonable. Name the GPU pool "gpu-inference-prod" with a taint key redwood/gpu=true:NoSchedule and use tolerations on serving pods. CPU pool should be "general-purpose" with burstable resource classes for workers. We'll provide pod affinity examples to keep KV cache near model pods.
- Audit & KMS: Our audit logs redact request bodies by default and can be configured to exclude sensitive fields. For keys, Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys via KMS connectors; HSM integration is supported through our on-prem agent but will require a short key-exchange session during install.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm a tentative preflight call window (30–60m) — Wed 2027-06-09 or Thu 2027-06-10 work for us.
2) Share cluster node specs (CPU/mem/disk) and network ACLs.
3) We'll run a short readiness runbook and produce an action list before the site visit.

Best,
Irene
Solutions Engineer, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

- Risks:
  * Network overlap with our hosted pools (we should confirm no public routability issues).
  * HSM integration may require on-site security approval and timeline impact.
  * Storage: if they opt for NFS instead of block-replication we'll need IO benchmarking.

Proposed activities:

2) Marcus to own storage sizing and provide a storageclass/Csi spec by EOD 6/9.
3) Solutions (Irene/Marissa) to produce the recommended node-pool manifest and taints/tolerations for the pilot by 6/10.
4) Engineering (Marcus) to validate KMS/HSM integration steps and flag any blockers by 6/11.

I'll brief CS and our field eng. Also looping a short on-site support quote if they want a day of hands-on assistance. Attaching deployment-roles.csv (internal).

-Marissa
